contracts.rule: `applyCollection` writes in an order a crash cannot hurt: the tombstones, then both manifests, then the files, then graph state. A file the mover cannot take keeps its row, so a stuck picture is never left unlisted.

A collection removes only the manifest rows nothing uses, decided per row and root. A row stays when it fills a slot the keep set lists, a kept slot's task drew it, the project or a graph file names it, it is a concept or a reference, or a kept row was drawn from it.

At the start of a run every task a previous owner left at `running` goes back to `pending` with `interrupted: true`, superseded versions included, and spends no failure budget. Each wave starts only ready tasks the current plan asked for.

`Task.error` holds why a task reached a terminal state other than `done`. The scheduler writes the runner's error on every outcome, so `done` clears it, and a failure also pushes a `TaskAttempt` that carries the same reason.

Once per run, after the failure retries and before the wave loop, every planned `done` or `needs_human` task whose bound generation graph has drifted goes back to `pending`, and `RunSummary.redrawn` names it. A successful redraw clears the drift.

The `shot_image` runner holds the P7 loop: each attempt draws, every configured reviewer critiques the picture against the shot spec, and a blocking merged verdict refines the prompt for another attempt, up to `max_refine_attempts`. Then the shot is `needs_human`.

`RunSummary.failed` and `needsHuman` are the tasks the last planning pass asked for that are in those states, not what this process ran, so a failure inherited from an earlier run still exits `vngen run` non-zero and an orphan is never reported.
A task's `checkpoint` names its execution journal. Resuming the task replays the successful image and review responses saved there, then makes only the requests that remain.

Once per run, after the first planning pass and before the wave loop, a planned `failed` task goes back to `pending` while it has fewer attempts carrying an `error` than `max_task_attempts` (default 2, one retry). `needs_human` is never requeued.

A stop takes effect before the next API request: requests in flight settle, their successful responses are saved before the runner reads them, and an unfinished task goes back to `pending`, marked interrupted, with no failure attempt.

A run given `RunOptions.only` starts only the ready tasks in `closureOf(graph, targets)`, the targets and every task they depend on, recomputed at each wave. Planning is unchanged; only which ready tasks start is.

Each task keeps a diagnostic log at `vngen/state/tasklogs/<hash>.jsonl`, gitignored because it holds full model prompts and replies. It is not provenance: writes are best effort, and a failed append never fails a task.

A live scene is not decomposed, and none of its slots is ready, until every character in `scene.characters` has an approved portrait: a portrait row that is both current and accepted. The solver applies it per unit; the stills family lists the cast's portraits.

Editing a generation graph bound to a slot moves no task hash, so it is reported as drift: the output node's authored hash differs from its last completed run's, or the node never ran and the graph is not the default one. `execution.redrawDrifted` redraws it.

A node in a generation graph is addressed by its key, the chain of ids from the root (`3/7` for node 7 inside instance 3), never by its id alone. The hashes, the journal, the executor's targets, the cost walk and every `gengraph.*` command's `node` prop use it.

An edit inside a group instance can only override a value; `decideGenEdit` refuses a structural edit there with the sentence `structuralEditsRefused` gives. Structural edits go to the group's definition, written as `vngen/work/graphs/lib/<ref>.json`.

Renaming a node type's socket or prop needs a migration in the same commit: bump the type's `typeVersion` and add a `NodeMigration` step that lands on it. `migrateGraphJSON` replays the renames over a file's JSON before `readGraphFile` deserializes it.

A concept image never gets a node in the task graph: `generateConcept` records a hash of the request (prompt, params, refs) as the asset's `sourceTask`, and nothing a run plans consumes the asset, so a project holding a concept plans exactly the tasks it planned before.

A shot's task inputs carry its location twice: `buildShotPrompt` names the location, and the plate's asset hash leads `refs`. So rewriting a scene's heading re-keys every shot in the scene, unlike retyping a line, which re-keys nothing.

`solve` enumerates a family's slots whether or not anything has been drawn, and attaches a task hash only to a slot whose kind can resolve its inputs now; any other slot carries the kind's sentence saying why. Edges come from each kind's `refs`, never from `Task.deps`.

A shot in a staging-sheet group carries `params.extra.sheet`, a hash of the sheet's prompt, its reference hashes in order and the group seed, so anything the sheet is drawn from re-keys every member at once. A shot in no group carries no `extra`.

A task is identified by `sha256(kind, inputs)`, where the inputs are the normalized prompt, the ordered reference asset hashes and the params, and never the model id. Identical work therefore collapses to one node.
Outside the scheduler, a `done` record is written only by adoption (`@vn/artgen/adopt`). The maintenance writers re-write a record the log already held, verbatim, or write `pending`.
Every status transition appends the whole task to `state/tasks.jsonl`, and replaying the log, last writer wins per hash, rebuilds the task graph.

A tombstone takes a task out of the replayed graph. It is a full copy of the task's last record with `status: 'pending'`, no `output`, no `error`, and `removed: true`, and a later record for the same hash supersedes it.

`planTasks` runs once per scheduler wave. It decomposes the owed scenes whose unit gate is open, solves the stills family, and adds the task of every slot the solver reports `ready`. It keeps no enumeration and no gate of its own.

Every authored character has a portrait slot and every authored location variant a plate slot, cast or not. Sheet slots exist only for the outfits `usedOutfits` finds over live scenes, so an uncast character has none even once approved.

A batch decomposition writes a storyboard only for a live scene with no `work/shots/<sceneId>.json`, has no `force`, and never writes a baseline: a scene the model does not answer for is named and skipped. Hosts refuse mock or unresolved keys by name.

Authored `artNotes` are appended to what a builder derived, entity note first and the narrower rung second, and an empty note adds nothing, so a project that authors no notes composes byte-identical prompts. A shot's prompt reads only the shot's own notes.

Art notes, image seeds and image models are authored at the same five rungs, addressed as `character:<id>[/<outfit>]`, `location:<id>[/<variant>]` or `shot:<sceneId>/<shotId>`, and every host writes them through one parser and one write path, with the same refusals.

A derived prompt is a `PromptChunk[]` of keyed clauses, which `renderPrompt` collapses to the flat string a task hashes. An override edits that list at the one rung naming the whole picture, and a project with no override composes byte-identical prompts.

P5 receives the scene as identified lines, `[<lineId>] <kind>/<speaker>: <text>`, never as flattened prose, and a decomposition that binds none of the scene's real line ids falls back to the baseline.

A storyboard is single frames or manga pages, as `shot_form` decides. A page's panels carry their own cast, drawn from the shot's, and their own lettered lines. Under `lettering: model` those lines are in the page's prompt and hash; a panel's bubbles are in no prompt.

A reference is a `ChunkRef` on one clause: muting the clause drops it, the task hashes its `pin` rather than its slot, authored refs follow the derived ones in `TaskInputs.refs`, and a ref with no `from` names an asset by hash and never drifts.
The reference graph over slots stays acyclic: `prompt.addRef` runs `refCycle` in its check and refuses a reference that would close a loop, naming the whole path. The cycle is over slots, not hashes.

The P7 reviewer sees only what `shotSpec` says about the shot: its own framing, location and cast, with the prose of its covered lines marked as context only. `spec.characters` decides who must be in frame, and an empty list means an absence is not a defect.

A model id alone picks its backend: it names a native vendor, gains a transport from the keys that resolve (the vendor's, else OpenRouter's, else none), and a model no key carries is refused by name before anything is paid for. The scheduler never imports a concrete provider.

The text steps (P1 location enrichment, P5 shot decomposition) call the LLM with structured-output enforcement and fall back to a deterministic baseline when the step fails, so a whole run completes with mock providers and no API calls.

The Gemini, Claude and OpenRouter backends retry a transient failure (429, 5xx or a transport error) in place, up to `ATTEMPTS` calls in all. Any other failure, an unrecognized one included, is terminal at once.

A character or set-location is a file whose front matter says `type: character` or `type: location`, found only in `characters/<id>/character.md`, `locations/<id>.md` and `wiki/**/*.md`, and it is read and written only in the file it was found in.

A character or location sheet's front-matter `id:` must equal the id its file's name implies (the directory for a character sheet, the filename stem elsewhere); a mismatch is an `entity_id_mismatch` error and the entity is dropped.

Editing a scene's heading through `setHeading` moves no line id and no coverage, restages every shot in the scene onto the new heading's variant, and counts those shots as `restaged`, never as `drifted`, in the price shown before the edit runs.

A linear project's scene order is `project.yaml`'s `scenes:` list and nothing else: never the directory's order, never branch markers. A listed id with no scene file, a repeat, a marker and a `start:` that is not the first listed scene are errors.
Line ids are allocated and stored, and a read never writes: a new line takes its id from its scene's allocator, never from its position, and loading a project allocates ids in memory only.

Whether a scene is live comes only from the model's narrative engine (`model.narrative.live`). The builder fills `model.reachable` and `model.entry` from it, and the production readers (planner, decomposition, slot graph, `usedOutfits`, gate) ask it rather than walk markers.

`outfitFor` alone resolves what a subject wears, in order: the shot subject's own `outfit`, then the scene's `[[outfit: id=outfit]]` marker, then the character's `default_outfit`. An absent field defers to the next level.

Editing a scene's prose never invalidates a frame's art, so drift is reported: `driftOf` compares the hash of a frame's covered lines, stamped with its image, against the same hash now, and a drifted frame's shot slot says so on `SlotState.drift`.
A scene edit that spans several chunk files is computed and proved in full before any file is written, and an existing chunk keeps its front-matter block byte for byte; only the body is rewritten.

A scene is one `scenes/<id>.md` file whose front matter is `scene: <id>` and nothing else and whose body is one complete Fountain scene with its own heading. The id comes from the filename and the front matter, and the body cannot override it.
Writing a scene to Fountain and parsing it back returns the same scene, `parse(write(scene)) ≡ scene`, for every field of `Scene`. `sceneToFountain` writes from `Scene.lines` and the heading fields.

`loadInputs` alone decides which files hold scenes, reading only `scenes/<id>.md`, and every scene writer patches the sources `sourcesOf` derives from the same `LoadedInputs` the model was built from, never from a second look at `scenes/`.

A shot has no position field: its place is where its covered lines sit. Moving a shot moves the block of lines it covers, through the scene write path, and only a contiguous shot can move; one with another shot drawing inside its lines is refused by name.

A base asset root whose directory exists without a readable manifest is `unavailable`, and the project is refused: `solve` reports the refusal with no slot ready, the planner plans nothing, and every act that would write to the root refuses in the same sentence.
Each asset root writes its manifest through one queue: a write waits for the previous one, re-reads the file, and applies only the rows its own instance changed.

A scene is decomposed once: the planner reads `work/shots/<sceneId>.json` whenever it exists and decomposes only when it does not. A malformed file throws, a dry run writes none, and a reader fills a copy of the model's `production` map rather than the planner's.

Image bytes are stored once per root under their content hash: base art (portraits, model sheets, plates, concepts, references) in `assets/`, shot frames in `vngen/build/`. A write routes by `AssetKind` alone, and each root has its own manifest.

A stills slot is approved when the take it holds (`pick`: its one current row, else its only row) is a row a person accepted. Every kind, the portrait included, answers through the one test on `SlotKind.approved`, `heldAccepted`.

A slot holds one take: its one `current` row, else its only row (the solver's `pick`). Two current rows hold nothing, and `overHeld` says which stays. `current` (the slot holds it) and `accepted` (a person approved it) are set by different acts, and neither clears the other.

A row is suspended when a pinned reference on it no longer names its slot's take, or when a row it was drawn from is suspended. `suspensions` derives that on every read and nothing stores it; a suspended row keeps its bytes and nothing is redrawn for it.
